angles.title: The independent who left: Duggan is off the ballot but still has a market price
angles.synopsis: Mike Duggan announced on May 21, 2026 that he was ending his independent campaign for governor. The Michigan Department of State's general election listing shows five governor candidates and no independent. Kalshi's governor event still lists a Duggan contract, last traded at 0.3 cents when we captured it on October 28. Benson and James are the two nominees; Marist's October 15-18 poll shows Benson ahead among likely voters.

sources.outlet: Michigan Department of State, Official Candidate Listing, General Election 2026-11-03
Marist Poll, Midterm Elections in Michigan

unknowns: Whether Duggan's name or petitions remain anywhere on file: the Bridge article does not say
Why the Kalshi contract is still listed (not stated by Kalshi)
Marist's governor question wording and exact percentages are not on the page we read

angles.title: Senate: a two-point poll and a 69-cent contract, side by side
angles.synopsis: Marist (Oct 15-18, 1,185 registered voters, multi-mode) has El-Sayed 50 and Rogers 48 among likely voters, margin of error 4.3 points. Other October polls reported by Political Wire (YouGov, Quantus, CBS Detroit/Mitchell) also show El-Sayed ahead, mostly within their margins. Kalshi's Senate contract for El-Sayed last traded at 69 cents on Oct 28 (bid 67, ask 69). A price is not a forecast and a poll is not a vote share; the piece shows both and explains the difference without predicting. It links to the money delta piece already live.

sources.outlet: Political Wire (YouGov, Quantus, CBS Detroit/Mitchell summaries)

unknowns: Original releases for YouGov, Quantus and Mitchell not opened
Marist likely-voter sample size is not stated on the page

angles.title: MI-13: an incumbent loses his primary and the Republican is a first-time candidate
angles.synopsis: Donavan McKinney beat Rep. Shri Thanedar in the August 4 Democratic primary, roughly 51.9 to 48.1 with 99 percent counted per Michigan Advance. The Republican nominee, T.P. Nykoriak, was unopposed. A search summary reports a 2016 federal sentence for Nykoriak; that needs the court record and a response attempt before any use.

angles.title: MI-10: the open seat both parties are targeting
angles.synopsis: John James left the seat to run for governor. Christina Hines (D) and Mike Bouchard (R) are the nominees. A search summary reports $500,000 in outside spending for Hines in July and both national committees targeting the seat. The official listing spells her first name Christina; some outlets print Kristina.
